speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: asked the Minister for Health (a) whether the Ministry monitors the number of young children injured through accidental burns each year; and (b) what measures are being taken to increase awareness among parents and caregivers of burn risks and how to prevent burns in the home.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Health)
text: In addition, burns prevention and first aid tips for caregivers are available at HPB’s Health Hub.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Parents and caregivers play an important role and they have to take the necessary precautions to protect their children from burns.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Most critically, parents should avoid allowing young children in kitchens where the risk of getting burns or scalds are high, due to the presence of hot objects.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: I was just wondering to what extent does HPB's advice to parents of young children, include the specific reference to burns prevention at home?

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: In short, the answer to the Member's question is, yes, it is very focused on places where such burn incidents happen, and that includes kitchen, living room and other places.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I am not sure whether there is data on this.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: But of those cases that the Parliamentary Secretary cited, does he have any data on how many are non-accidental in nature?

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: That means is it related to abuse or suspected abuse?

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Maybe the Member could file a separate Parliamentary Question.
